chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the obligatory circumambulation of the Kaaba but did not know whether he had performed seven or eight circuits. He said: 'As for the seven, he is certain of them, and his doubt fell only on the eighth, so let him pray two rak'ahs.' And whoever doubts and does not know whether he performed six, seven, or eight, then it is obligatory upon him to repeat the circumambulation until he is certain that he has performed seven circuits. He narrated that.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one is unsure whether they performed 7 or 8 rounds of Tawaf?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* distinguishes between 'doubt' (shakk) and 'certainty with residual doubt' (istiqran) in the context of Hajj rituals. It establishes that minor uncertainty regarding an extra circuit does not invalidate the obligatory act, whereas significant ambiguity among multiple possibilities necessitates a full repetition to ensure the validity of the pillar.
